parties: <cite index="1-1,7-6">Oriental Hotels Limited (an associate company of The Indian Hotels Company Limited) merging with and into IHCL</cite>
headline: <cite index="3-7,3-10">IHCL approves merger of associate Oriental Hotels via all-stock scheme at 25:117 share ratio, targeting second-half FY2028 completion with appointed date of April 1, 2027</cite>
sum: Oriental Hotels Limited merges into India's largest hospitality company (IHCL) by Scheme of Arrangement, with share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares on all-stock basis, completion targeted in second half of FY2028.
implication: <cite index="5-17,5-18">Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 of Companies Act 2013 requires NCLT sanction plus shareholder, creditor, stock exchange and SEBI approvals-a multi-gated restructuring requiring careful statutory sequencing and timing management</cite>.
detail: <cite index="7-6,7-7">Oriental Hotels is an associate company of IHCL with a portfolio of seven hotels and 825 rooms</cite>, <cite index="7-8">including freehold assets Taj Coromandel–Chennai, Taj Fisherman's Cove Resort & Spa–Chennai, Gateway Coonoor, and leasehold assets Taj Malabar Resort & Spa–Cochin, Vivanta Coimbatore, Vivanta Mangalore, Gateway Madurai</cite>. <cite index="5-9">IHCL held 37.05% of OHL's equity as of June 30, 2026</cite>. <cite index="7-2,7-3">The scheme is subject to statutory approvals and clearances and proposes simplifying the group's holding structure by increasing IHCL's direct ownership, resulting in two new operating subsidiaries</cite>.

framework.note: central - Scheme of Arrangement requiring NCLT sanction and creditor/shareholder meetings for merger/amalgamation
central - Related-party transaction disclosures and approvals required given IHCL's 37.05% pre-existing stake
central - NCLT Order required under Section 232 to sanction the scheme after creditor/member meetings
Tax neutrality for amalgamation subject to conditions; independent verification required post-sanction
Stock exchange approval and disclosure filings required for scheme implementation
Stamp duty on NCLT order varies by state (2–5%); multi-state asset portfolio triggers cumulative duty
Post-scheme filing and compliance for 210 days per annum under Form CAA.8 until scheme is fully implemented

structure.consideration: <cite index="3-1,3-4">25 IHCL equity shares (face value Re 1 each) for every 117 OHL equity shares (face value Re 1 each)</cite>; all-stock transaction
conditions: <cite index="8-3">Shareholder and creditor approvals of both companies as may be directed by NCLT</cite>
<cite index="8-3">Stock exchange and SEBI regulatory approvals</cite>
<cite index="27-11">Related-party transaction approval under SEBI Listing Regulations (IHCL holds 37.05% pre-existing stake)</cite>
structure.novel: <cite index="2-5,2-6">Consolidation of an existing 37.05% associate holding into full ownership, simplifying group structure and creating two new operating subsidiaries directly under IHCL</cite>; <cite index="25-11">OHL transitioned to 20-year Hotel Management Agreements with IHCL effective August 1, 2026, preceding the merger announcement</cite>.

triggers.note: Mandatory NCLT-supervised scheme for merger/amalgamation; triggers full court-supervised process
Related-party transaction: IHCL as 37.05% shareholder and promoter of OHL requires RP approvals and fairness opinion
Material event disclosure and scheme implementation notices to stock exchanges (BSE/NSE)
